title: Mars: Giant Volcanoes and a Great Canyon

pages.text: Mars has a great volcanic region called Tharsis. Huge volcanoes rise above its plains. One of them is bigger than all the others.

quickWords.th: ภูมิภาคภูเขาไฟ
ทาร์ซิส
ที่ราบ

pages.text: This is Olympus Mons. It is the largest known volcano in the Solar System. It is so huge that we need to look from far above to see its shape.

quickWords.th: โอลิมปัสมอนส์
ใหญ่ที่สุด
ระบบสุริยะ

pages.text: Olympus Mons is not a narrow, pointy mountain. It is a giant shield volcano with wide, gentle slopes. Its base is more than 600 kilometres across.

quickWords.th: ภูเขาไฟรูปโล่
ทางลาดไม่ชัน
600 กิโลเมตร

pages.text: Long ago, lava flowed across Olympus Mons again and again. The lava spread far over the ground. Layer by layer, the volcano grew wider and higher.

quickWords.th: ลาวา
ไหล
ทีละชั้น

pages.text: At the top are huge pits called calderas. Magma once moved away from below the summit. Then parts of the ground collapsed and sank.

แมกมา
ยอดเขา

pages.text: Mars has another giant landform. This is Valles Marineris, a vast system of canyons. It cuts across thousands of kilometres of Mars.

quickWords.th: ภูมิลักษณ์
วัลเลสมาริเนริส
หุบผาชัน

pages.text: Some parts of Valles Marineris are hundreds of kilometres wide. The deepest places reach about nine kilometres down. Its cliffs expose layer after layer of Martian rock.

quickWords.th: ลึกที่สุด
หน้าผา
หินบนดาวอังคาร

pages.text: Mars has changed over billions of years. Water flowed. Volcanoes grew. Canyons and craters recorded its history. Today Mars is cold and dry, but its old landscapes still tell us what happened long ago.
